text:
maya: FYI customer reported sudden 3x P99 latency and throughput drop for their Private (VPC) cluster about 15:05 UTC.
maya: traces show lots of retries and model kernel selection falling back to single-threaded kernels.
sam: seeing same in infra metrics — egress NAT CPU spikes and conntrack table near max on their NAT instances.
liam: can you paste netstat/tcpdump? suspect MTU/fragmentation causing retransmits.
maya: attaching quick tcpdump snippet: 
```
14:58:23.456 IP 10.0.12.34.443 > 10.0.8.21.52345: Flags [P.], seq 1:1451, ack 1, win 29200, length 1450
14:58:23.457 IP 10.0.12.34.443 > 10.0.8.21.52345: frag (DF), length 2000
```
maya: also iptables had MSS clamp rule added by customer firewall team recently.
kai: that MSS clamp will break path MTU discovery over the NAT if not right — causing kernel to fragment or drop, TCP retransmits => higher service tail latency.
eng-runtime-oncall: profiling runtime when this happened showed a jump in KV cache eviction rate and increased kernel-selector 'fallback' count (preferring legacy conv kernels). Batching window grew because requests were stalling.
sam: conntrack state: `ss -s` and `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` showed near nf_conntrack_max=65536, conntrack exhausted transiently. NAT CPU exhausted handling conntrack lookups on fragmented packets.
liam: so chain reaction: MSS clamp + NAT hairpin -> fragments -> conntrack expensive -> NAT CPU spike -> packets delayed -> runtime sees slow responses -> kernel selector judges high latency and changes kernels -> small batches and kv-cache churn -> throughput drops.
maya: customers using private deployment with our VPC egress path are impacted. Need quick mitigation steps.
kai: immediate mitigations: 1) ask customer FW to remove/adjust MSS clamp to preserve PMTUD, 2) increase nf_conntrack_max to 262144 as short-term, 3) enable TCP MSS correction on NAT gateway if available, 4) add conntrack hashsize bump.
liam: ops-bot triggered runbook: `incident:private-egress-latency` with checklist — we're running canary changes.
eng-runtime-oncall: on runtime side we can: 1) temporarily reduce max_batch and max_wait_ms to prevent large batching windows and reduce tail amplification, 2) pin kernel selector to prefer stable vectorized kernels for affected model versions, 3) increase KV cache TTL to avoid premature evictions.
sam: applying conntrack bump on staging NAT now: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` and `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_buckets=65536` — will monitor.
maya: telemetry after change: NAT CPU down ~45%, conntrack_count back to safe range, P99 dropped from 1.2s -> 320ms within 10m.
kai: still see some fragments in tcpdump; customer FW says they must keep MSS clamp for policy reasons. Need permanent fix: either ensure MSS clamp uses 1460 or move NAT into path that honors PMTUD, or adjust our kernel selection to be fragmentation-aware.
liam: proposal for longer term: 1) add a kernel-selection feature flag that penalizes kernels when network-layer retransmits/fragmentation detected (use netlink/tc qdisc counters), 2) change batching heuristic to be adaptive to observed packetization delay instead of only service latency, 3) KV cache metrics: emit eviction reason tags to trace evictions back to network stalls.
eng-runtime-oncall: created follow-up ticket: INFRA-9273 "Frag-aware kernel selector + adaptive batching" and assigned to eng-runtime + eng-infra.
maya: action items before EOD: confirm customer FW can relax MSS clamp OR we push a canary kernel selector pin + conntrack increase. Kai/sam to coordinate with customer network team.
kai: coordinating now with customer; they can try MSS=1452 for testing. Will report.
maya: thanks everyone. I'll update customer and leave this thread open until final remediation. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: alert cleared for private-cluster-74 after conntrack bump and kernel pin applied on canary nodes.
